transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15
Time: 16:00 - 16:55 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (Redwood CSM), Sofia Reyes (EmberTech Head of AI), Marcus Lang (EmberTech Platform Eng), Priya Nair (CTO), Daniel Cho (SRE)
Recording: zoom.us/recording/abc123 (note: auto-generated)

Summary:
High-level QBR covering usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents for last quarter, and roadmap alignment. Customer expressed interest in exploring Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and tighter network controls (VPC). Security and SOC2 were discussed; Redwood to share package. Agreed next steps around benchmark runs and pricing follow-up.

Topics:
- Monthly token usage and cost breakdown
- Recent latency and tail events; SLOs
- Roadmap alignment and feature requests (longer context, caching behavior, model variants)
- Dedicated vs Hosted evaluation and VPC/on-prem needs
- Security/compliance docs (SOC2, SSO, KMS)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Tuesday afternoon, appreciate you carving time out. quick roll call?
[00:05] Sofia Reyes: Hi, Sofia here.
[00:07] Marcus Lang: Marcus on platform.
[00:08] Priya Nair: Priya here.
[00:10] Daniel Cho: Daniel, SRE.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Great. Liam and Jared from Redwood?
[00:14] Liam O'Connor: Liam here.
[00:15] Jared Kim: Jared joining.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Okay, high level agenda: usage/costs, reliability incidents, roadmap alignment, dedicated capacity ask and security package. we'll leave 10 minutes for next steps. sound good?
[00:25] Priya Nair: Yep, sounds good.

[02:15] Maya Patel: Alright, jumping into the usage slide — EmberTech has been steady at ~1.2B tokens per month with spikes up to 2.1B during release windows. Our cost breakdown shows embeddings and chat generation are the biggest drivers — embeddings cost has grown 34% q/q. does that match what you're seeing on your side?
[02:35] Sofia Reyes: yeah that's accurate, embeddings for vector search indexing during daily reindex jobs. we tried to reduce frequency but search quality drops so we keep it nightly. also note we have batch jobs in the early hours that create a big delta.
[02:48] Marcus Lang: to add, we also ran a pilot where we doubled context to 8k for some agent workflows which bumped token counts. surprised by the cost there, obviously.
[03:01] Liam O'Connor: right, that matches — longer context increases both compute and memory, but there are some caching levers we can use. Redwood Optimize recommendations suggested caching prefixes for those agent flows to reduce re-tokenization.
[03:16] Priya Nair: can you walk through the caching suggestion a bit? how much saving are we looking at?
[03:22] Liam O'Connor: sure, so if your agent flow reuses a stable prompt prefix per user session we can keep the KV cache and avoid re-sending same tokens; conservative estimate is 20-40% token savings on those flows depending on reuse. with batching and quantization profiles we expect additional 10-25% saving.
[03:38] Daniel Cho: is any of that on the hosted plan or do we need Dedicated to get KV cache persistence?
[03:45] Liam O'Connor: KV caching can be used on hosted but Dedicated gives more control over cache lifetimes and memory sizing — so for very large contexts, Dedicated plus configured caching profiles gives best predictability.

[06:00] Maya Patel: next up reliability — last quarter we had two incidents that impacted tail latency around 99.9th percentile during peak spikes; one was a burst cause by a misconfigured batch job. Daniel, you raised an SLO question in the ticket. can you summarise the impact you felt?
[06:18] Daniel Cho: on our side it manifested as elevated end-to-end p99 from ~600ms up to 2.2s for about 12 minutes, which caused timeouts in some internal orchestrator retries and downstream back-pressure. It was brief but amplified because retries stacked. logs attached to ticket.
[06:36] Jared Kim: thanks Daniel — we pushed a mitigation (auto-throttle) within Redwood runtime and implemented a fallback model variant to keep requests moving. root cause was noisy neighbor batch spikes + a suboptimal autoscaling threshold. we've since adjusted autoscaler and added a per-customer burst cap.
[06:55] Sofia Reyes: good to hear. curious on SLOs — what are realistic p95 and p99 numbers we can expect on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[07:04] Liam O'Connor: Hosted typically targets p95 under 300-400ms on standard models, p99 can be 700-1200ms depending on context length; Dedicated with pinned GPU pools can get p99 down to ~400-600ms for your 2k flows and better for smaller contexts. very dependent on seq length and batch strategies.
[07:22] Priya Nair: and tail latency for 8k contexts?
[07:25] Liam O'Connor: longer contexts push p99 a lot higher — think 1-2s on hosted; Dedicated with optimized kernels and KV persistence will be closer to 700-900ms in many cases but needs benchmarks. hence our action to run a 4k/8k bench with your sample prompts.

[10:10] Marcus Lang: question on observability — we saw a spike where correlation id disappeared between tracer and Redwood logs. can we get more trace retention or a mapping export?
[10:20] Jared Kim: yes, we can increase trace ingestion retention and share screenshots of the console. we also have a tracing hook so you can seed your trace ids; will include in the security pack how we surface logs and audit trails.

[12:30] Maya Patel: moving to costs — we modelled Hosted cost today vs Dedicated with a 6-month commit. in example scenarios Dedicated reduces unit cost by ~30-45% at your throughput but requires a commit and some setup. We've included burst capacity plans to handle release windows.
[12:50] Priya Nair: what's the minimum commit typically?
[12:54] Maya Patel: typical entry is a monthly committed vGPU pool size; for your usage we'd recommend starting with a mid-sized pool (equivalent to 16 A100-ish vGPUs or similar) and scale with auto policies. pricing spreadsheet will show ACU/slot math.
[13:08] Sofia Reyes: we need clearer math on cost vs spike events — if we undercommit we hit overage and then costs can be unpredictable.
[13:15] Maya Patel: totally — that's why we proposed a hybrid: Dedicated base + hosted burst fallback. that way you get predictability for most traffic and fallback when you spike.

[15:45] Daniel Cho: security — we need SOC2 type II, SSO via SAML, RBAC controls, and KMS integrations. also requirement for audit logs for two years and data residency EU controls for some customers. can Redwood meet all that?
[15:59] Jared Kim: yes, Redwood is SOC2 and we have a SOC2 package; we also support SAML SSO and RBAC. for KMS we support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations in Private/Dedicated deployments. audit log retention can be configured; we'll include the options in the packet and a sample retention policy. for EU data residency we can route to EU region or run Private deployment if required.
[16:25] Priya Nair: how different is Private vs Dedicated from our perspective?
[16:29] Liam O'Connor: Dedicated is still managed by Redwood but provides reserved capacity within our infra with VPC peering options; Private gives control of the control plane to you and can be deployed within your VPC or on-prem — it's more involved but meets stricter regulatory controls.

[20:02] Sofia Reyes: roadmap alignment — we need longer context support (8k+), better caching behavior for agents, and improved embedding pricing. any timeline on model variants or quantization options?
[20:18] Liam O'Connor: roadmap is to ship better quantization profiles and model variants optimized for latency/cost in Q3; extended context support is an ongoing engineering workstream — we expect improvements and early access for Dedicated customers in late Q3/early Q4. I'll mark that as a priority for your account.
[20:35] Marcus Lang: would Dedicated customers get early access?
[20:37] Maya Patel: yes, typically Dedicated or Private customers in pilot get early access and roadmap influence.

[24:10] Priya Nair: merchant question — are there any showstopper limitations for our use case if we stay on Hosted for the next 6 months while we evaluate Dedicated?
[24:20] Liam O'Connor: no showstoppers — Hosted will work, but you'll see more variance in tail latency and less control over KV persistence. if predictability is critical for checkout-like flows, Dedicated is recommended.

[28:00] Maya Patel: ok let's recap the risks: cost spikes from embeddings and long context, tail latency during peak spikes, and compliance/residency for EU customers. mitigations: caching, quantization, Dedicated baseline + hosted burst, autoscaler tuning, and security packet.

[33:40] Sofia Reyes: one behavioral note — during our Black Friday simulation we had an emergent pattern where retries from our job scheduler caused compounding spikes. would Redwood consider a per-customer circuit-breaker?
[33:52] Jared Kim: yes, we have per-customer burst caps and circuit-breaker rules we can apply; we also provide request-level throttling hooks for your scheduler to honor.

[38:15] Maya Patel: I'm going to propose concrete next steps now: 1) we'll share QBR deck + updated pricing (Maya) 2) run performance benchmark on your sample prompts for 4k and 8k (Liam) 3) you share usage CSV + spike windows (Priya/Sofia) 4) Redwood shares SOC2/security packet and trace retention options (Jared) 5) schedule Dedicated scoping the week of 2026-06-22.
[38:45] Priya Nair: agreed. can you include example commit scenarios with cost math?
[38:50] Maya Patel: yes, that's in the pricing spreadsheet.

[43:05] Marcus Lang: quick question on telemetry retention costs — you said we can choose retention tiers, what's the delta?
[43:12] Jared Kim: typically retention tiers increase cost linearly; 90 days vs 1 year is about 1.6x, 2 years about 2.8x — exact numbers in the pack but we'll include sample screens.

[47:30] Daniel Cho: ops question — if we go Dedicated, what's the failover story for region outages?
[47:38] Liam O'Connor: we recommend multi-region Dedicated pools or a Dedicated primary with hosted fallback across regions. there are also automated fallback policies to a compatible model variant in another region. we'll provide an architectural doc.

[51:00] Priya Nair: last question — are there SLAs for cold-start or model load times?
[51:08] Maya Patel: SLA typically covers availability and request success; cold-starts are operational and we have runbooks to minimize them — Dedicated reduces cold starts due to pinned pools. we'll include specifics in the SLA appendix.

[53:30] Maya Patel: ok thank you everyone. we'll send the deck and pricing and the security pack by Wednesday, Liam will run the bench and share results next week, and we'll pencil in scoping for week of June 22.
[53:48] Sofia Reyes: thanks all. appreciate the clear next steps.
[53:55] Priya Nair: thanks, bye.
[53:58] Maya Patel: thanks, bye.
